This gates write actions, not reads: every view stays public, so the first real controllers to call it are the EPIC-9 role actions (lineups, call-ups, trades, contracts), not the existing read-only endpoints — it has no request-spec coverage of its own yet, the same way authenticate_user! never did; both get proven through their first real caller.

A league_admin can act on any team within their league without a team-level membership row

description: league_admin, gm, assistant_gm, coaching_staff.

Migrations for League, Team, Season
Migration + model for TeamAffiliation (hierarchical team relationships)
description: Self-join on Team: parent_team_id, affiliate_team_id, season_id (season-scoped rather than started_on/ended_on, matching how Season already anchors history elsewhere). Models the NHL/AHL/ECHL affiliate chain (e.g. Ottawa Senators -> Belleville Senators). Backfilled via ImportTeamAffiliations, which reads each AHL/ECHL manifest's nhl_affiliate abbreviation and anchors to the newest NHL season on hand.

title: Seed NHL, AHL, and ECHL teams as real Team rows
description: Adds abbreviation/logo/colors to teams, drops the unused city column, and loads data/{nhl,ahl,echl}-teams/teams.json (94 teams) via the ImportTeams service, keyed on abbreviation so reruns update rather than duplicate. Team logos copied into frontend/public/teams/<league-slug>/. Affiliation backfill from nhl_affiliate belongs to TASK-17.

title: Seed the three leagues and list them on the dashboard
description: Adds abbreviation/tier/logo to leagues, seeds NHL/AHL/ECHL, exposes GET /api/v1/leagues scoped by membership (Super Admin sees all), and renders them on the dashboard home page. League SVGs copied from data/ into frontend/public/leagues/.

title: League detail page: click into a league, see its teams
description: GET /api/v1/leagues/:slug returns one league with its teams (404 rather than 403 when the caller can't see it, so the endpoint doesn't confirm existence). Frontend route /leagues/:slug -> LeaguePage container, TeamCard component, useLeague model. Dashboard league cards link into it.

title: Move league/team logos into Active Storage
description: Logos were files committed to frontend/public, so changing one meant a frontend redeploy. Now has_one_attached :logo on League and Team, Disk service (S3-compatible later), seeded from data/ via AttachLogo with a checksum guard so reruns don't orphan blobs. Serializers emit absolute proxy URLs; the logo filename columns are dropped. SVG is served inline via a documented exception to Active Storage's binary-serving default — revisit if an upload endpoint is added.

title: Super Admin logo upload
description: There is no way to fix a bad logo without editing data/ and re-seeding — Seattle's had to be replaced by hand on 2026-08-22. Needs PATCH /api/v1/teams/:id/logo and /leagues/:slug/logo restricted to Super Admin, content-type and size validation, plus a frontend control. Note the Active Storage caveat in docs/DECISIONS.md: uploads make the SVG-served-inline exception unsafe, so sanitize SVG on the way in or rasterize.

title: NhlClient: throttled, retrying HTTP client for api-web.nhle.com
description: Net::HTTP, no new runtime gem. Process-wide minimum interval on a monotonic clock, exponential backoff on 429/5xx/timeout capped at 3 attempts, 404 not retried, typed errors. Paired with a single-threaded ingest queue in config/queue.yml.

title: Sync services and jobs for seasons, standings, and games
description: SyncSeasons, SyncStandings, SyncTeamSchedule, SyncDailyScores, sharing UpsertGame. All upsert on natural keys so reruns are safe, and all report unmatched teams instead of skipping silently. Wrapped by jobs on queue_as :ingest.

title: Backfill task and daily recurring syncs
description: rake 'nhl:backfill[20242025,20252026]' loaded 3,001 games and 64 standings rows in ~2 min. Daily standings + scores at 9am UTC in recurring.yml. Widening the season range is a re-run, not a code change.

title: Read API for standings and team games, plus docs/API.md
description: GET /leagues/:slug/standings (season + date params, dated snapshots) and GET /teams/:id/games (season + game_type). Scoped by League.visible_to and User#authorized_for_team?; unauthorized reads as 404. docs/API.md covers our endpoints and the upstream ones we consume.

title: Migrations for skater_game_stats and goalie_game_stats
description: Renamed from SkaterStatLine/GoalieStatLine. Two separate tables, not one wide nullable table. Grain is (player, game), with team_id on the row itself (not inferred) so a mid-season trade attributes each game to the right club. Field scope confirmed against a live /v1/gamecenter/{id}/boxscore response — see DECISIONS.md. Season/league/career totals are a SUM over these, not stored here; see TASK-44 for the read-side cache. Depends on TASK-8 (Player, RosterEntry).

title: Design Player/RosterEntry schema
description: Settled. Global players keyed on nhl_player_id, player_external_ids for every other source (with matched_by provenance), roster_spots (player+team+season+contract_level) rather than a current-team FK, and team_affiliations for the NHL/AHL/ECHL chain. Contracts deliberately left orthogonal. See docs/DECISIONS.md.

title: Migrations for players, player_external_ids, roster_spots
description: Plus hockeytech_team_id / hockeytech_season_id on teams and seasons, both uniquely indexed per league rather than globally — AHL and ECHL ids may share a namespace. Draft columns (year/round/overall/team) ride along on players since both upstreams send them structured.

title: Design Game/SkaterStatLine/GoalieStatLine schema
Migrations for Game + stat line tables
description: Game table shipped with NHL ingestion (nhl_game_id, season, home/away teams, type, venue-local date, scores, state, last period type). SkaterStatLine/GoalieStatLine remain outstanding — tracked as TASK-26.

title: rails new --api, wire up Docker Compose (backend + db)
Health-check endpoint + first RSpec smoke test
Decide Vite vs Next, scaffold app + Tailwind
description: Vite + React + TS + Tailwind v4 scaffolded, @ alias wired in tsconfig.app.json and vite.config.ts. Folder structure settled as containers/components/models/auth/lib (see docs/DECISIONS.md) — the earlier features/api layout was replaced.

title: Login screen wired to backend JWT
description: LoginPage posts to /api/v1/login, AuthProvider stores the JWT and hydrates identity from /me; RequireAuth and RedirectIfAuthenticated own both directions of the redirect.

title: Super Admin UI: move a player between teams, edit records
Decide external stats data source
description: Settled: the NHL's public web API (api-web.nhle.com), catalogued at github.com/Zmalski/NHL-API-Reference. Replaces the dead statsapi.web.nhl.com the prior attempt used. See docs/DECISIONS.md.

title: Migration and seed data for team_affiliations
description: parent_team_id / affiliate_team_id / season_id, named to avoid colliding with teams.nhl_team_id (an external id). Season-keyed so a moved affiliation doesn't rewrite history. Toronto needs both tiers: Marlies (AHL) and Cincinnati Cyclones (ECHL). Hand-maintained in data/. Data was already present in every manifest (nhl_affiliate) and just needed reading — no hand-authored seed data required.

title: HockeyTechClient for the AHL and ECHL roster feeds
description: Same construction as NhlClient — process-wide throttle, capped backoff, typed errors, jobs only. Public statview keys: ahl/ccb91f29d6744675, echl/2c2b89ea7345cae8. Verified live: roster's trailing element is always a nested array of coaching staff, not an error case, so the client hands the raw array back and callers filter to Hash entries. A blank team_id silently returns every team's roster concatenated upstream, so the client raises instead. A 200 with a plain-text "Invalid key." body (or a malformed-prefix error body seen on other views) is caught and re-raised as InvalidResponse rather than an uncaught JSON::ParserError.

title: SyncTeamRoster and SyncAffiliateRoster
description: NHL org roster from /v1/roster/{team}/current (follows a 307). Affiliate rosters from HockeyTech, AHL before ECHL — the ECHL feed sends status empty, so contract_level is inherited from the AHL row and flagged inferred. Match on normalized name + birth_date, report missing_players. Falls back to the newest season that actually has a roster, since the current one is empty until camp. Verified live against real data: NHL org roster (49 players), Marlies (50, 26 NHL/15 AHL/6 PTO/3 ATO — exact match to discovery), Cincinnati Cyclones (51, Kressler's NHL contract correctly inherited). Live run also surfaced a real cross-feed data disagreement (HockeyTech's AHL and ECHL rosters disagree on one player's birthdate), caught by the new possible_duplicates report rather than silently forking his identity — see docs/DECISIONS.md.

title: GET /teams/:id/roster
description: Grouped by position, carrying contract_level and the affiliate chain so an NHL team's page can show who is on assignment. Headshot URLs derived, never stored. GET /teams/:id/roster: TeamRoster query (app/queries) resolves each org player's current AHL/ECHL assignment by season date-range overlap, batched into one query. PlayerSerializer/RosterSpotSerializer derive headshot_url, never store it. Verified with a request spec covering the assignment case; live confirmation on real data is blocked by an unrelated dev-data timing gap (org roster synced under 2026-27, affiliates still on 2025-26) — code path confirmed correct via spec with matched seasons.

title: Model retained rights (drafted-but-unsigned players)
description: Wants its own player_rights table, not a roster_spots row — a rights-held player is not on a roster in a season, and forcing him into one would model a lie. Needs name matching against players who may have no nhl_player_id yet. Unbuilt because no complete source exists: /v1/prospects/{team} returns only drafted-and-unsigned-abroad (4 players for Toronto, all KHL), and /v1/draft/picks/{year}/all carries no playerId, only name and amateur club.

title: Persist possible-duplicate player pairs from roster syncs
description: possible_duplicate_players (player_a, player_b, detail, resolved_at), player_a always the lower id so a rerun can't double-write the same pair. SyncAffiliateRoster writes a row when a same-normalized-name entry disagrees with an existing player's birthdate, alongside the existing possible_duplicates log line. Prompted by a real live find: HockeyTech's own AHL and ECHL feeds disagree on Rhett Parsons's birth month.

title: Team page: side-nav dashboard (Overview/Schedule/Roster)
description: TeamPage becomes a shell (header, theme, side nav) rendering nested routes via Outlet: /teams/:id (Overview), /teams/:id/schedule, /teams/:id/roster. Overview shows last-3/next-3 games, computed client-side from the existing full-season fetch (no new endpoint). Roster consumes GET /teams/:id/roster, grouped Forwards/Defensemen/Goalies, showing jersey number, position, and an assignment badge when a player is currently on an AHL/ECHL affiliate. GameRow extracted from ScheduleList so Overview's summary cards reuse it rather than duplicating the outcome-badge logic. 'Leading players' deferred with Overview's layout, pending SkaterStatLine/GoalieStatLine (TASK-26) — not stubbed, not referenced. Verified live in a headless browser: real Toronto data, 49-player roster correctly grouped, no console errors.

title: Design Lineup schema and its active/historical visibility rule
description: Lineup belongs to Team + Game, not roster_spots: starting goalie, forward lines, defense pairings, scratches. Needs an explicit active/historical distinction, history-preserving like roster_spots rather than a single mutable 'current' row. Once a game starts (or ends — TBD which), the lineup stops being a hidden, team-private draft and becomes a normal visible game record; before that, only members of the owning team can see it. v1 eligibility is gated on roster_spots.team_id alone (current team assignment) — not a real 23-man Active Roster / Injured Reserve / Non-Roster distinction (Article 16), which is TASK-40. Known simplification, not an oversight — see docs/DECISIONS.md.

title: Coach: set a team's lineup for a game
description: A coach-role Membership on a team can create/update that team's own Lineup for a game. Depends on TASK-35 (schema) and TASK-3 (authorization foundation). v1 doesn't check whether a named player is actually within the 23-man Active Roster or on Injured Reserve (TASK-40) — only that he's on the team.
acceptance_criteria: A coach can set/edit their own team's lineup for a game
A coach on one team cannot edit another team's lineup, including a same-league opponent
Any member of the owning team can view its active (not-yet-played) lineup
A user outside the owning team cannot view an active lineup, but can once it's historical

title: GM: call up / send down players across a TeamAffiliation
description: Reassigns a roster_spots row between a parent team and its affiliate (existing TeamAffiliation, TASK-28). Authorization is hierarchical, not peer-to-peer: the acting GM's team must be the parent_team in a TeamAffiliation row for the current season where the affiliate_team is the target player's team. The affiliate's own GM cannot initiate the same move. Depends on TASK-3. v1 doesn't check Regular Waiver exemption (Article 13) — a veteran being sent down in real life would often need to clear waivers first, where other clubs can claim him. That's TASK-43.
acceptance_criteria: The parent team's GM can move a player to or from its affiliate for the current season
The affiliate team's GM cannot move a player to or from its parent
A move attempted outside an existing TeamAffiliation edge is rejected

title: GM: propose and respond to trades with other teams
description: New Trade entity: proposing team, receiving team, the players/assets on each side, and a pending/accepted/rejected/withdrawn lifecycle. Unlike call-ups, this is peer-to-peer — either side's GM can propose, regardless of any TeamAffiliation relationship between the two teams. Depends on TASK-3. Biggest unknown of the EPIC-9 tickets: the schema and state machine aren't sketched yet.

title: GM: register a player contract
description: New Contract entity (term, value, level) tied to Player + Team + Season. A GM can register a contract for a player rostered on their own team. Depends on Player/roster_spots (EPIC-3) and TASK-3. Registering a contract here does not enforce cap legality — Team Payroll Range compliance (Article 50.5) is EPIC-10, deliberately layered on top rather than bundled in.

title: GM: place a player on injured reserve or non-roster
description: roster_statuses (player, team, season, status: injured_reserve/non_roster, started_on, ended_on) — day-scoped and history-preserving like the rest of the roster domain. 'active' is never stored; a player with no open period is active by default, so the common case needs no row at all. A GM sets it via PATCH /teams/:id/roster_statuses/:player_id (role_key: gm, TASK-3), for a player already on that team's roster (found via roster_spots, which also supplies the season). started_on/ended_on can be backdated to today or earlier — real IR placements are often reported after the fact — but never future-dated. Moved from EPIC-3 to EPIC-9 once scoped: no external feed reports this, so it's a role action, not ingestion. Does NOT yet enforce the 23-man Active Roster max (16.4) or wire into TASK-36's lineup eligibility or EPIC-10's cap accounting — the table exists, nothing consumes it yet.

title: Team Payroll Range enforcement: Averaged Club Salary, Upper/Lower Limit
description: Article 50.5. Averaged Club Salary is calculated daily — the sum, for each day of the season, of every rostered/IR/non-roster player's Averaged Amount, with a two-way player's NHL portion prorated by the fraction of the season actually spent on the NHL roster. Not a static season-long sum of cap hits. Depends on TASK-39 (Contract must exist) and TASK-40 (day-scoped roster status).

title: Bona-Fide Long-Term Injury/Illness Exception (LTIR)
description: Article 50.10(d). Lets a Club exceed the Upper Limit when a Player is unfit to play for 24+ calendar days and 10+ NHL games: replacement salary is capped at the injured Player's own salary, and the Club must return to Upper Limit compliance before he's activated again. Depends on TASK-41.

title: Waiver-exemption tracking for send-downs
description: Article 13. Waiver exemption is age-at-draft and games-played based (e.g. an 18-year-old drafted skater is exempt for 3 seasons or until his 160th NHL game, whichever comes first). Past exemption, sending a player to the minors requires clearing Regular Waivers, where any other Club can claim him — TASK-37's call-up/send-down currently assumes this never happens.

title: Migrations for skater_season_stats and goalie_season_stats (recomputed cache)
description: Read-side cache on top of TASK-26's game-grain tables, keyed (player, team, season, game_type) — same grain as roster_spots, so a traded player gets one rollup row per team stint. League and career totals are a further SUM over these rows rather than over every game. Recomputed from *_game_stats after each write in the same ingestion job, not incremented in place, so a corrected boxscore or out-of-order backfill can't drift it. Exists purely for read performance (leaderboards, career totals) — never hand-edited, never the source of truth. See docs/DECISIONS.md.

title: Boxscore ingestion: UpsertGameStats, RecomputeSeasonStats, SyncGameStats
description: NhlClient#boxscore (/v1/gamecenter/{id}/boxscore). UpsertGameStats parses one boxscore into skater_game_stats/goalie_game_stats rows, attributing team_id from which side of the payload a player is listed under (not roster_spots), and reports missing_players (unmatched nhl_player_id) rather than raising, same shape as SyncAffiliateRoster's missing_players. RecomputeSeasonStats re-sums *_game_stats into the TASK-44 cache for every (player, team, season, game_type) touched. SyncGameStats + SyncGameStatsJob (queue_as :ingest) wire both together for one game at a time. Verified against a trimmed real boxscore fixture, including the goalie strength-split "saves/shots" string format and toi "MM:SS" to integer-seconds conversion.

title: Backfill and daily recurring sync for game stats
description: TASK-45's SyncGameStatsJob syncs one game at a time, on demand — nothing yet calls it for every already-finished game (rake nhl:backfill doesn't touch it) or wires it into recurring.yml alongside SyncDailyScoresJob. One boxscore request per game means a full-season backfill is ~1,300 requests at the client's throttled 1 req/sec (~20+ min) — worth deciding batching/scope before wiring it in, not just looping every Game.find_each.

title: SyncRun / SyncRunItem schema
description: sync_runs: scope description (league/season/team, all nullable as appropriate), sync_kinds requested, status enum (queued/running/completed/failed/cancelled), total_steps, current_step, current_step_label, min_interval used for the run, started_at/finished_at, error_message, triggered_by_id (FK users). sync_run_items: sync_run_id FK, team_id FK (nullable — standings/daily-scores have no team axis), kind, status enum, started_at/finished_at, error_message. Models with associations, enums, a percent_complete helper.
acceptance_criteria: percent_complete handles total_steps == 0 without dividing by zero
A SyncRun with zero items still has a sensible default state (queued, 0%)

title: Api::V1::Admin::BaseController with require_super_admin!
description: New Api::V1::Admin::BaseController < Api::V1::BaseController, before_action :require_super_admin! reading as one question (current_user.super_admin?) the same way BaseController#authorize_team! already does. Routes: namespace :admin under /api/v1 with sync_runs (index/show/create, member :cancel).
acceptance_criteria: A request spec proves a non-super-admin user gets 403 on every admin route
A super admin passes through with no Membership row required

title: Registry mapping each sync kind to its valid scope axes
description: Roster/affiliate-roster/schedule take a team (+season for schedule); standings/daily-scores are league+date with no team axis; game-stats is per-game. A small registry (kind -> {service class, required scope axes}) is the single source of truth the orchestrator (TASK-50) and the trigger form (TASK-53) both read, so the UI never offers a team picker for a kind that doesn't take one.

title: AdminSyncOrchestratorJob
description: queue_as :ingest. Resolves the requested scope into a team/date list via TASK-49's registry, creates SyncRunItem rows, flips SyncRun to running, then loops calling the matching existing service (e.g. SyncTeamRoster.new(team:, client: NhlClient.new(min_interval: sync_run.min_interval)).call) directly — no new job classes for the existing six. Increments SyncRun.current_step atomically (UPDATE ... SET current_step = current_step + 1, not a Ruby read-modify-write) and sets current_step_label after each item; captures a failing item's error without aborting the run; checks for a cancelled status before starting each new item. Design decision (loop-in-process vs. fan-out to the existing per-team jobs) logged in DECISIONS.md.
acceptance_criteria: A job spec against stubbed services proves current_step ends at total_steps with correct per-item labels
A spec proves the atomic increment doesn't lose updates — this is the failure mode that actually matters here
A spec proves a run marked cancelled mid-loop stops before its next item instead of finishing

title: Admin::SyncRunsController: index/show/create/cancel
description: index (recent runs + counts), show (progress + a capped jsonb activity log appended to by the orchestrator — nothing external to scrape logs from), create (validates scope against TASK-49's registry, builds a queued SyncRun with the chosen min_interval, enqueues AdminSyncOrchestratorJob), cancel (queued/running -> cancelled). Goes through render_data/render_error like every other endpoint, not a bare render json:. Serializers in app/serializers.
acceptance_criteria: Request specs for all four actions, including the 422 case for an invalid scope/kind combination

title: Admin nav entry + Sync Dashboard page
description: Admin entry in UserMenu.tsx, rendered only when the current user is super admin (confirm is_super_admin is actually serialized to the frontend user payload — it may not be yet). New src/containers/Admin/ (folder, not a flat file, since it owns child routes the way TeamPage does) with a SyncDashboardPage listing recent runs. New src/models/adminSync.ts + useSyncRuns hook + a queryKeys entry, following the request-fn/hook split. Route guarded by a super-admin equivalent of RequireAuth.

title: New Sync trigger form
description: Cascading league/season/team fields that show or hide per the selected kind (per TASK-49's registry — reflect it as a small typed TS constant reviewed against the Ruby side, or expose it from the API; worth deciding at implementation time rather than presupposing here), a rate-limit preset selector mapped to min_interval, posting to the create endpoint.

title: Live progress view with polling
description: SyncRun detail page using React Query's refetchInterval (~1.5s) while status is queued/running, stopping once terminal. Renders progress bar, current-step label, per-item grid, and log tail per the Data Sync Console mockup. Cancel button posts to the cancel endpoint.

title: Contextual single-team resync
description: A Resync action on a team's existing page, pre-filling the trigger flow to that one team and posting straight to create.

title: Self-healing player identity in UpsertGameStats
description: Real gap found running the admin sync console against live 2026-27 data: a player who left a team's org before rolling off appears in that team's game logs/stats for a season he played but is permanently invisible to us, because the only thing that ever creates a Player row (SyncTeamRoster) syncs /v1/roster/{team}/current — present-tense only, never a past season. Once a player is off every current roster, no existing sync path can ever discover him again, so UpsertGameStats#player_for finds no match, skips the stat row, and reports the id in missing_players. This isn't timing (won't self-resolve when the season rolls over) and isn't rare (a full-season vet who's since left an org and a one-game-of-career call-up hit the exact same code path). Fix: on a miss, UpsertGameStats fetches NhlClient#player_landing (new client method, /v1/player/{id}/landing) to create a real, fully-populated Player on the spot, and also upserts a RosterSpot for (player, team, season) using the team/season already known from the game/boxscore context — contract_level: unknown (existing enum value, never yet used) and contract_level_inferred: true (existing flag, currently only ever set false), so it reads as inferred rather than authoritative. RosterSpot::SOURCES needs a new value (nhl_api/hockeytech/manual don't honestly describe "inferred from a stat line, not a roster feed"). UpsertGameStats needs a client: passed through from SyncGameStats (it doesn't take one today). missing_players should then only ever report an id the landing lookup itself couldn't resolve (e.g. a 404), not merely "wasn't already known." Deliberately out of scope: a full historical-roster pull from club-stats/{team}/{season}/{gameType} (participation data) — that only adds coverage for a player who was rostered all season but never dressed for a single game, which self-healing can't catch since it never sees a boxscore for him. Shelved unless zero-game roster completeness actually becomes a real product need; see DECISIONS.md for the full reasoning.
acceptance_criteria: A boxscore player id with no matching Player creates one via the player-landing lookup instead of skipping the stat row
The newly created player also gets a RosterSpot for (team, season) with contract_level: unknown and contract_level_inferred: true, not just a bare Player row
missing_players only reports an id when the landing lookup itself fails, not merely because the player wasn't already known

title: Goalie goals/assists are structurally unrepresentable
description: A goalie can record a goal (shooting into an empty net) or an assist — rare, but real, and currently lost entirely: goalie_game_stats has no goals/assists columns, and neither does goalie_season_stats (the recomputed cache), so there's nowhere for UpsertGameStats#upsert_goalie or RecomputeSeasonStats#upsert_goalie to write them even if they tried to — this is a schema gap, not a dropped value in the ingestion code. Fix mirrors what skaters already do at both layers: add goals/assists integer columns (default 0) to both tables, set them in upsert_goalie from row.fetch("goals", 0)/row.fetch("assists", 0) exactly like upsert_skater already does, and sum them into the season cache in RecomputeSeasonStats#upsert_goalie the same way skater goals/assists are already summed. Before locking in field names: the one boxscore fixture on hand doesn't show goals/assists keys on the goalie row at all, but that's almost certainly because it's a scoreless-for-that-goalie game (fixtures are trimmed by dropping whole teams/games, never by editing fields), not evidence the API omits those keys generally — same discipline TASK-45's original field scope used ("confirmed against a live boxscore response rather than assumed from docs") should apply here: pull a real boxscore from a game where a goalie actually recorded a point before committing to the shape.
acceptance_criteria: Field shape (goals/assists keys on a goalie's boxscore row) verified against a real live boxscore from a game where a goalie recorded a point, not assumed from the trimmed fixture
A goalie's goals/assists are captured in goalie_game_stats the same way SkaterGameStat already captures a skater's
goalie_season_stats.goals/assists are recomputed from goalie_game_stats the same way skater season totals already are

title: Migrations + models for game_events and shifts
description: Raw per-game event tables — the source data the rollup tables in this epic get computed from, though nothing populates them yet (no ingestion in this task). game_events: one row per play-by-play event (shot, goal, faceoff, hit, giveaway, takeaway, penalty, blocked_shot). References game, team (nullable — not every event has a clean team attribution), primary_player (required), secondary_player (nullable, for assists/blockers/drawn-by). Columns: nhl_event_id (bigint, unique scoped to game_id, same upstream-key-for-re-sync convention as Game#nhl_game_id), period, period_time_seconds, event_type, shot_type, zone, strength_state, x_coord, y_coord. shifts: one row per player per on-ice stint. References game, player, team. Columns: nhl_shift_id (unique scoped to game_id), period, start_time_seconds, end_time_seconds. event_type/shot_type/zone/strength_state are small closed sets — model as explicit hash constants (Game::GAME_TYPES / RosterSpot::CONTRACT_LEVELS pattern), not free strings.
acceptance_criteria: nhl_event_id and nhl_shift_id are unique per game, not globally — matches the natural-key-per-scope pattern hockeytech_team_id/hockeytech_season_id already use
primary_player is required on game_events; secondary_player and team are nullable

title: Migration + model for xg_models (versioned xG coefficients)
description: Versioned xG coefficient sets a future model-computation step reads from — no training/fitting logic here, just the table. Columns: version (unique), coefficients (jsonb), trained_at, active (boolean). Exactly one row may be active at a time; enforce with a partial unique index (WHERE active) rather than a model validation alone, so a race between two activations can't leave two actives — the same reasoning already applied elsewhere in this schema to hard invariants a validation alone can't guarantee.
acceptance_criteria: A partial unique index, not just a model validation, makes two simultaneously-active rows impossible even under a race
Activating a new version and deactivating the previous one is one atomic operation, not two writes that could interleave

title: Migration + model for player_game_advanced_stats (per-game rollup)
description: Materialized per-game advanced-stat rollup — recomputed wholesale, never live-computed at read time and never hand-edited, same philosophy as skater_game_stats/goalie_game_stats (TASK-26). References game, player, team, xg_model (the coefficient version that produced this row's xG figures, so a later re-run with a newer model is traceable). Columns: strength_state (default "all"), corsi_for/against, fenwick_for/against, xg_for/against, zone_entries, zone_exits, toi_seconds. Unique index on (game_id, player_id, strength_state) — a player gets one row per strength state per game ("all", "5v5", "pp", ...), not one row per game. Depends on TASK-59 for the xg_model_id FK.
acceptance_criteria: Unique index on (game_id, player_id, strength_state) lets the same player hold separate "all" and "5v5" rows for one game without colliding
xg_model_id is required, not nullable — a row's xG figures are meaningless without knowing which coefficient version produced them

title: Migration + model for player_season_advanced_stats (chained running-total snapshots)
description: Running-total snapshot per player/season, one row per game boundary rather than per calendar date — each row's totals are the prior row's totals plus that game's delta, so the rows chain rather than each being an independent recompute (contrast with skater_season_stats/goalie_season_stats, TASK-44, which re-sums from scratch every time). References player, team, season, as_of_game (→ games). Same stat columns as player_game_advanced_stats (TASK-60) plus games_played. Add stale (boolean, default false) — flipped true when an earlier game in the chain gets corrected, cleared once the chain is rebuilt forward from that point (TASK-63). Unique index on (player_id, season_id, strength_state, as_of_game_id). Depends on TASK-60.
acceptance_criteria: Unique index on (player_id, season_id, strength_state, as_of_game_id) prevents two snapshot rows from claiming the same point in a player's chain
stale defaults false and is a plain flag on the row — nothing computes off it besides TASK-63's job deciding what needs rebuilding

title: Migration + model for team_game_advanced_stats (per-game team rollup)
description: Materialized per-game team-level advanced-stat rollup — same recomputed-never-live-computed strategy already used everywhere else in this schema (skater/goalie game+season stats, player_game/season_advanced_stats), applied at team grain rather than a GROUP BY over player rows at read time. Confirmed against hockey-reference's team gamelog page, which shows team-level CF/CA/CF%/FF/FA/FF%/oZS%/PDO per game alongside the basic box score line — that's this table's shape, not something derived on the fly. References game, team. Columns: strength_state (default "all"), corsi_for/against, fenwick_for/against, xg_for/against, faceoff_wins/losses, pdo, toi_seconds — same column shape as player_game_advanced_stats (TASK-60) where it overlaps, plus the team-only PDO/faceoff figures the gamelog page shows. Unique index on (game_id, team_id, strength_state). Depends on TASK-60 for the sibling shape.
acceptance_criteria: Unique index on (game_id, team_id, strength_state) — one row per team per strength state per game
Nothing computes this at read time from player rows — it's populated by the same recompute job as player_game_advanced_stats (TASK-62)

title: Migration + model for team_season_advanced_stats (per-season team rollup, recomputed from scratch)
description: Season-level team rollup — unlike player_season_advanced_stats (TASK-61), this needs no chained snapshots: a team can't get traded mid-season the way a player can, so there's no cross-entity game-order-chaining problem to solve. Recomputed from scratch from team_game_advanced_stats after every relevant write, same pattern as skater_season_stats/goalie_season_stats (TASK-44) — a full re-sum bounded by one team's season (≤~82 games), never incremented in place. References team, season. Columns: strength_state (default "all"), corsi_for/against, fenwick_for/against, xg_for/against, faceoff_wins/losses, pdo, toi_seconds, games_played. Unique index on (team_id, season_id, strength_state). Depends on TASK-66.
acceptance_criteria: Recomputed wholesale from team_game_advanced_stats, never incremented in place — matches skater_season_stats/goalie_season_stats's existing recompute discipline
Unique index on (team_id, season_id, strength_state)

title: Recalculation job: rebuild the stat chain forward from a corrected game
description: Add stats_syncing (boolean, default false) to games. MarkGameForStatsRecompute flags games.stats_syncing = true and that game's affected players' player_season_advanced_stats rows from that game forward as stale = true, then enqueues RebuildAdvancedStatsJob (queue_as :ingest). RebuildAdvancedStatsForGame rebuilds each affected player's player_season_advanced_stats chain forward via RebuildPlayerAdvancedStatsChain (ordered by the player's actual games through player_game_advanced_stats, not calendar date, so a cross-team affiliate stint chains correctly) and re-sums team_season_advanced_stats for both teams via RecomputeTeamSeasonAdvancedStats, then flips games.stats_syncing back to false only once every affected player's chain and both teams' rollups are rebuilt. Rebuild = delete the stale tail and reinsert it chained off the last untouched snapshot, never incremented in place, so a partial run followed by a full re-run can't double-count a game's delta. Scope note: this assumes player_game_advanced_stats/team_game_advanced_stats for the corrected game are already fresh by the time this runs — the actual computation of those per-game rows from game_events/shifts (on-ice attribution, xG-from-coordinates via xg_model) is real domain logic nothing in the schema defines yet, and is out of scope here; see TASK-72.
acceptance_criteria: A spec proves rebuilding a player's chain from a corrected mid-season game produces the same final totals as a from-scratch recompute of every game in order
A spec proves the job is safe to re-run: interrupting it partway and re-running from the top never double-counts a game's delta
A spec proves chain order follows the player's actual games, including a cross-team affiliate stint, not calendar date
games.stats_syncing is false again only once every affected player's chain has been rebuilt, not after the first one completes
A spec proves both teams' team_season_advanced_stats are re-summed from team_game_advanced_stats by this same job run

title: Surface stats_syncing in team games / player stats API meta
description: Per the existing { data, meta? } envelope: team games and any endpoint touching a game currently mid-recalculation include stats_syncing in meta when true, matching the existing convention that meta carries derived/pagination info and is omitted rather than sent false when there's nothing to say — so the frontend can show a "recalculating" state instead of silently serving numbers that are about to change. Depends on TASK-62.
acceptance_criteria: A request spec proves meta.stats_syncing appears when the underlying game has stats_syncing: true, and is absent (not present-and-false) otherwise

title: Score-state (close/all) advanced stat splits — recompute from stored events, no new NHL calls
description: Hockey-reference slices advanced stats by score-state ("close" — within one goal in the 1st/2nd, tied in the 3rd — vs. all situations) in addition to strength_state, doubling every strength-state table (All/EV/PP/SH/5v5 x close/all-score). Deliberately out of v1 scope (TASK-60/61 ship strength_state only) — more surface than a hockey-reference-inspired v1 needs. Cheap to add later specifically because score-state is derivable entirely from data TASK-58 already stores: the score at any event reconstructs from goal-type game_events rows already in the table, so this is a new aggregation dimension over already-ingested game_events/shifts, not a new api-web.nhle.com integration or client call. Adding it means a score_state column/dimension on player_game_advanced_stats/player_season_advanced_stats (or a sibling table) plus a one-time backfill recomputing score-state-filtered rollups for every game already ingested by then. Depends on TASK-58/60/61/62.
acceptance_criteria: The backfill recomputes score-state splits for already-ingested games using only stored game_events/shifts — no NHL API call is made
The backfill is safe to re-run, same requirement TASK-62's forward-chain rebuild already has

title: Wire advanced-stats ingestion/recompute into the admin sync console
description: Once play-by-play/shift ingestion (deferred, not part of this epic) and TASK-62's recompute job exist, a super admin needs to trigger them the same way every other sync kind already works — through EPIC-12's SyncKindRegistry / AdminSyncOrchestrator / New Sync trigger form, not a separate one-off mechanism. Add a new sync kind (or kinds) to SyncKindRegistry with its required scope axes (team + season, matching team_schedule/game_stats), have AdminSyncOrchestrator dispatch to whichever ingestion/recompute service this epic's ingestion task and TASK-62 land as, and let it show up in the existing New Sync form as just another kind option — no new frontend page. Depends on the actual ingestion path and TASK-62 existing first; this task is only the admin-console wiring.
acceptance_criteria: The new kind appears in GET /api/v1/admin/sync_kinds with its scope axes, the same shape every existing kind already returns
Triggering it from the existing New Sync form enqueues the same recompute path a corrected-game trigger (TASK-62) would use, not a separate code path

title: Query objects for league-wide skater/goalie search, filter, sort, pagination
description: New app/queries/ objects (matching RosterStatusPage/GameDatePage's existing hand-rolled offset-pagination style, not a pagination gem) building the read for a league-wide (or per-league) player list: name search (ilike), filters (league, team, position, season, game_type), sort on any column from a fixed allowlist spanning both skater_season_stats/goalie_season_stats and player_season_advanced_stats (TASK-61) — never an arbitrary client-supplied column/direction string, same discipline as never interpolating raw SQL. Skaters and goalies get separate query objects, not one merged query — matches the rest of this schema's skater/goalie separation. Depends on EPIC-13 (player_season_advanced_stats) for the advanced-stat columns.
acceptance_criteria: Sort column/direction are validated against a fixed allowlist — an unrecognized column is rejected, not silently interpolated into ORDER BY
meta shape (page/per_page/total_count/total_pages) matches RosterStatusPage's existing convention rather than inventing a new one

title: GET endpoints for league-wide skater/goalie search
description: Controllers wiring TASK-68's query objects to routes, request params validated against the same allowlists, response following the existing { data, meta } envelope. Each row serializes both basic and advanced stat columns. Depends on TASK-68.
acceptance_criteria: Request specs cover search, at least one filter, sort (including an invalid-column 422), and pagination

title: Extend DataTable with server-side pagination and filtering row models
description: TanStack Table's pagination and filtering row models — explicitly deferred at DataTable's original build (docs/DECISIONS.md) for exactly this use case. DataTable needs a server-driven mode: pagination state comes from the backend's page/per_page/meta (TASK-69), not a client-side row model operating over an already-fetched full array, since a league-wide list is hundreds of rows and can't be fetched whole up front. Existing SkaterStatsTable/GoalieStatsTable usages (team-scoped, small row counts, client-side sort) must keep working unchanged — this is an added mode, not a rewrite of the existing one. Depends on TASK-69.
acceptance_criteria: Existing team-scoped DataTable usages (SkaterStatsTable/GoalieStatsTable) are unaffected — same client-side sort behavior as today
A server-driven table correctly reflects the backend's current page/total without re-fetching or re-sorting client-side

title: League-wide player search page
description: New page wiring TASK-69's endpoints through TASK-70's extended DataTable: a search input, filter controls (league/team/position/season), sortable columns spanning basic and advanced stats, and pagination controls. Separate skater/goalie views (tabs or separate routes), not a merged table. Depends on TASK-70.

title: Compute player_game_advanced_stats/team_game_advanced_stats from game_events + shifts
description: The per-game computation TASK-62's recompute job assumes is already done: given a game's game_events and shifts, determine which players were on the ice for each event (via shifts' start/end times), bucket by strength_state, and derive Corsi/Fenwick (shot-attempt counts by on-ice player), xG (apply the active xg_model's coefficients to each shot's x_coord/y_coord), zone entries/exits, and TOI — then upsert player_game_advanced_stats for every player who was on the ice and team_game_advanced_stats for both teams. This is the actual hockey-analytics algorithm deferred out of TASK-62 (see its scope note) because nothing in the schema defines it yet and it's a substantially larger, more novel piece of logic than the chain-rebuild mechanics. Depends on real game_events/shifts ingestion existing (also not yet built — see EPIC-13's description) or, for development, fixture data shaped like it.
acceptance_criteria: Given game_events/shifts for a game, on-ice attribution correctly identifies which skaters were on the ice for each event using shift start/end times, not just event team
xG per shot is computed from the currently-active xg_model's coefficients against that shot's x_coord/y_coord
Output upserts player_game_advanced_stats for every player on the ice and team_game_advanced_stats for both teams, matching the existing tables' strength_state bucketing

title: Validate XgFormula's coordinate-frame assumption against real ingested play-by-play
description: XgFormula (TASK-72) assumes x_coord/y_coord are already relative to the attacking net at (89, 0) — a documented v1 simplification, since real NHL coordinates are absolute rink position and which end a team defends flips by period, and there was no real ingested play-by-play yet to check the convention against (see docs/DECISIONS.md's TASK-72 entry). Once real play-by-play ingestion exists and game_events actually holds NHL data, verify whether the assumption holds. If NHL coordinates are absolute rink position (the expected case), XgFormula needs a per-period, per-team normalization step (flip x_coord based on which end that team defends that period) before computing distance/angle, and this task also updates the DECISIONS.md entry once resolved. Depends on real play-by-play/shift ingestion existing (deferred, not part of EPIC-13). Superseded by TASK-75: homeTeamDefendingSide (confirmed present on every real play-by-play event) made this a fix, not a validation exercise — XgFormula.calculate now takes target_net_x:, resolved per event from that field, with a spec proving identical xG for the same physical shot regardless of which end is defended.
acceptance_criteria: Compares XgFormula's output against a sample of real ingested game_events and confirms whether the (89,0)-relative assumption holds or needs per-period/per-team normalization

If normalization is needed, XgFormula (or a wrapper) correctly flips coordinates by attacking end before computing distance/angle, with a spec proving a shot from the same physical spot scores the same xG regardless of period or which end the team defends
docs/DECISIONS.md's TASK-72 entry is updated to reflect the resolved (not simplified) coordinate handling

title: NHL play-by-play + shift-chart client methods
description: Add play-by-play (likely /v1/gamecenter/{id}/play-by-play on api-web.nhle.com, same host NhlClient already talks to) and shift-chart (historically a separate host — api.nhle.com/stats/rest/en/shiftcharts — unverified, needs checking against a live response the way every other endpoint in this codebase was confirmed before being trusted, not assumed from third-party docs) client methods. If the shift-chart host really does differ from api-web.nhle.com, this may need its own client class (same reasoning as HockeyTechClient being separate from NhlClient), not a bolted-on method on the wrong client.
acceptance_criteria: Both endpoints' actual response shapes are confirmed against a live call, not assumed from docs
Follows the existing client conventions: throttled via min_interval, retried on 429/5xx, no retry on 404

title: UpsertGameEvents / UpsertShifts services
description: Parse a game's play-by-play response into game_events rows and its shift-chart response into shifts rows, upserting on the natural key (nhl_event_id/nhl_shift_id scoped to game_id — TASK-58's existing convention). Report unmatched players the way UpsertGameStats already does via missing_players, not by raising or silently skipping. Depends on TASK-74. Incorporates findings from that research (see docs/DECISIONS.md): filter shift-chart rows to typeCode 517 (real shifts), discarding typeCode 505 goal-marker noise; skip play-by-play types not modeled (period-start/end, stoppage, delayed-penalty, game-end); derive strength_state per event from situationCode (away vs. home skater-count comparison) rather than guessing; parse "MM:SS" shift start/end times the same way parse_toi already does. Add GameEvent::SHOT_TYPES[:between_legs] (real data has it, schema doesn't) and GameEvent#tertiary_player (nullable, class_name: "Player") for a goal's second assist. Fix XgFormula's coordinate normalization using each event's homeTeamDefendingSide instead of the TASK-72 placeholder assumption, since the parser already needs that field for zone/coordinate attribution — this supersedes TASK-73.
acceptance_criteria: Re-running against the same payload is a no-op (upsert, not append) — matches every other ingestion path in this codebase
An event/shift referencing an unrecognized player is reported, not silently dropped or a hard failure
A spec proves XgFormula's fixed normalization scores the same physical shot location identically regardless of which end the team defends that period

title: Wire real ingestion through to the advanced-stats recompute pipeline
description: The composition TASK-72 was deliberately left un-wired for: a job that calls UpsertGameEvents + UpsertShifts, then ComputeGameAdvancedStats, then MarkGameForStatsRecompute for one game — same shape as SyncGameStats composing UpsertGameStats + RecomputeSeasonStats today. Decide during implementation whether this extends the existing admin sync console 'advanced_stats' kind (TASK-65) to do real ingestion now instead of MarkGameForStatsRecompute alone, or is a second kind — TASK-65's kind currently assumes computation already happened, which stops being true once this exists.
acceptance_criteria: Triggering ingestion for a real game populates game_events/shifts, then player_game_advanced_stats/team_game_advanced_stats, then rebuilds the season-grain rollups, in one traceable run
Re-running for the same game is safe, consistent with every other recompute in this schema

title: Validate the advanced-stats pipeline against real ingested games
description: On-ice attribution, Corsi/Fenwick counts, and score-state classification (TASK-72/64) have only been proven against synthetic spec fixtures — never a real game. Once TASK-76 can ingest real data, spot-check a handful of real games' computed Corsi/Fenwick/score-state splits against a public reference (e.g. Natural Stat Trick or MoneyPuck for the same game/date) and fix whatever discrepancies turn up — shift-boundary edge cases, strength-state mapping gaps, event-type coverage. Complements TASK-73, which is the narrower xG-coordinate-frame half of this same validation effort.
acceptance_criteria: At least one real game's computed Corsi/Fenwick totals are compared against a public reference source and match within a documented, understood tolerance
Any real discrepancy found is fixed or explicitly logged as a known, documented gap — not silently left

title: Game detail/boxscore page (frontend)
description: No per-game detail page exists at all today — games only appear as list rows (team schedule, league games, GameSerializer). Build one, showing the existing basic skater/goalie game stats plus the new advanced-stats splits (player_game_advanced_stats/team_game_advanced_stats) once real data exists via TASK-76. Needs a backend endpoint serving one game's full stat picture, which doesn't exist yet either — nothing currently serves a single game by id with its stat lines attached.
acceptance_criteria: A game detail page renders basic stats today and advanced-stats splits once TASK-76 provides real data, not before
Backend endpoint follows the existing envelope/serializer conventions

title: Extend TeamStatsPage with an advanced-stats view
description: TeamStatsPage already renders season skater/goalie basic stats. Add a view for team_season_advanced_stats (and, per player, player_season_advanced_stats) — strength_state/score_state as filters or tabs, matching the dimensions those tables already carry. The lower-lift half of the frontend work here, since the page and its data-fetching pattern already exist.
acceptance_criteria: Team stats page can show advanced-stats splits by strength_state/score_state alongside the existing basic stats, once real data exists

title: Player detail page with season-by-season stats
description: No per-player detail page exists yet. Build one showing season-by-season basic and advanced stats (skater_season_stats/goalie_season_stats plus player_season_advanced_stats), inspired by the hockey-reference player-page review done for EPIC-13's frontend scoping. Sequencing note: EPIC-14's league-wide player list is a separate concern (search/filter/sort/paginate), but its rows should link here once both exist.
acceptance_criteria: A player's page shows season-by-season basic stats today, and advanced-stats columns once real data exists via TASK-76

title: Train a real xG model to replace the placeholder coefficients
description: The active XgModel ("v0-placeholder") has made-up coefficients (intercept: 0.2, distance: -0.05, angle: -0.02), not fitted ones — confirmed visibly wrong live (TOR @ ANA, 2026-03-30 showed 10.55-12.10 combined team xG; a real NHL team's xG per game is typically 2-4). The pipeline mechanics (on-ice attribution, per-shot formula application via XgFormula, home_team_defending_side coordinate normalization) are correct — only the coefficients are meaningless. Needs a real logistic regression (or similar) fit against historical shot data with actual goal/no-goal outcomes, using distance-to-net and angle-to-net as features (matching XgFormula's existing two-feature shape, or widening it if a real fit calls for more features e.g. shot_type, strength_state, rebound/rush indicators — that's a model-design decision for whoever builds this, not decided here). Once trained, XgModel.activate! swaps it in atomically, no other code changes needed. Depends on enough real game_events existing to fit against (TASK-74/75/76 ingestion, run across enough real games).
acceptance_criteria: A newly trained XgModel's per-team-per-game xG totals fall in a realistic range (roughly 1-6 per team per game) against a sample of real ingested games, not the placeholder's inflated numbers
The training process and feature choices are documented (in DECISIONS.md or alongside the training script) so the coefficients aren't a black box

title: Build the component library admin page
description: A new route under /admin (Super Admin only, same guard as AdminPage's other pages) that imports every presentational component in frontend/src/components and renders each with a couple of representative prop combinations — e.g. Text's every variant/tone, SegmentedControl with 2-4 options and a selected value, DataTable with a few sample rows and columns built via buildColumns, badges in each of their states. One section per component, in a scannable list (mirrors AdminPage's existing SideNav shape rather than inventing new admin layout). No new component variants or props needed to ship this — it's a page that exercises what already exists.

title: Multiselect teams on the New Sync Run form
description: Real gap found recovering from a stuck sync run (TASK-56/57 era mass game_stats pull, interrupted by a machine restart mid-run): 6 of 32 NHL teams needed a follow-up sync, and NewSyncRunPage's team picker only takes one team at a time, forcing 6 separate trips through the form. Explicitly scoped as frontend-only, no backend/schema change: SyncRun stays one-team-or-whole-league per run exactly as it is today (a real multi-team-in-one-run redesign was considered and deliberately rejected here as more than this needed — see chat log/DECISIONS.md if revisited). Fix: turn the team <Select> into a multiselect; on submit, loop useCreateSyncRun once per selected team_id (same sync_kinds/season_id/preset each time) instead of a single createSyncRun call. Selecting zero teams keeps today's behavior (whole-league run) so this is additive, not a breaking change to the single-team case.

title: Dev has no real job queue: sync runs can't survive an interruption, and concurrent jobs deadlock each other
description:
Root cause found across two separate real incidents: development has no configured active_job.queue_adapter, so it falls back to Rails' true default, :async — an in-process thread pool tied to the puma process's own lifetime, with zero persisted execution state and no per-queue concurrency limit. config/queue.yml's ingest queue (processes: 1, threads: 1, specifically so NHL syncs can never run in parallel and burst the client's rate limit) is entirely inert under :async; it's only honored by Solid Queue, which only production actually uses (config/environments/production.rb sets queue_adapter = :solid_queue). Four consequences, not one: (1) a machine/editor restart mid-run kills the job with nothing left to resume it — sync run 10 hung at 83% this way, status stuck at running forever; (2) AdminSyncOrchestrator#call iterates every sync_run_item unconditionally and always re-runs it (a plain .each, no status filter), so even a correctly-retried job would blindly redo every already-completed team rather than resuming; (3) worse, and already actively happening under normal, uninterrupted operation: MarkGameForStatsRecompute enqueues RebuildAdvancedStatsJob per game and returns immediately rather than rebuilding inline, so as the orchestrator's single thread marches through one team's games, several of that team's RebuildAdvancedStatsJobs end up executing concurrently on :async's thread pool — each rewriting player_season_advanced_stats rows for the same shared roster in a different order. Real PG::TRDeadlockDetected errors resulted, roughly half of San Jose's 88 games failing in one run, and got steadily worse the deeper into a whole-league run it went. Root of that pattern: RebuildAdvancedStatsForGame rebuilds chains for players from *both* teams in a game and recomputes both teams' season rollups, and a whole-league advanced_stats run processes every game twice by design — once from each team's own schedule (games_for matches home or away) — so a shared game (e.g. ANA @ COL) gets fully reprocessed a second time once the other team's turn comes around. That second pass touches a much wider, already-built chain than the first fresh pass did, so collisions (and therefore failures) climb as more of the league accumulates chain data and as :async's unbounded, unserialized job backlog grows over the run's duration — not a steady rate. Not data corruption (a deadlock rolls back, doesn't partially write), but real, frequent sync failures during totally normal admin-console use, not just during a rare interruption. (4) Worst for actually using the app while a sync runs: :async doesn't fork a separate process, it runs jobs on another thread inside the same Puma process — and Puma dev runs single-process (WEB_CONCURRENCY unset), 3 threads (RAILS_MAX_THREADS unset). Every thread in a Ruby (MRI) process shares one GVL, so the job's CPU-bound work (JSON-parsing full play-by-play/shift-chart payloads, ComputeGameAdvancedStats' in-memory math, RebuildPlayerAdvancedStatsChain's per-player rebuilding) competes for the same GVL as Puma's own request-handling threads. Confirmed live: dashboard became unresponsive mid-sync while pg_stat_activity showed only 2 DB connections, neither blocked — not DB load, the web threads just weren't getting a timeslice. Fix needs three parts, not two: run development on Solid Queue as a genuinely separate process (bin/jobs run standalone — NOT the SOLID_QUEUE_IN_PUMA plugin, which embeds the worker in the same process and would fix nothing here, since it's still one process/one GVL), which also makes config/queue.yml's existing single-consumer ingest queue actually take effect and eliminates the deadlock scenario; plus make AdminSyncOrchestrator skip already status: completed items so a retried/resumed job doesn't redo finished work — a partially-done per-game item is safe to simply re-run from its first game, since UpsertGameStats/UpsertGameEvents/RebuildAdvancedStatsForGame are already natural-key upserts.

Implemented: development.rb sets queue_adapter = :solid_queue + solid_queue.connects_to (matching production); database.yml gained a queue: entry for development/test, using db/queue_schema.rb that already existed for production; Makefile's make start now runs bin/jobs as its own process alongside Rails/Vite, make init uses db:prepare so the new queue db gets provisioned; docker-compose.yml gained a worker service (doc'd as a gap in ARCHITECTURE.md before this). AdminSyncOrchestrator#call now skips items already status: completed on a resumed run. Local caveat found while verifying, and actually fixed: on this machine, bin/jobs's default fork mode reliably segfaults on fork (EXC_BAD_ACCESS in the pg gem's C extension via libxpc — a macOS-only fork()-then-syscall bug class). Ruled out the precompiled gem's vendored libpq as the cause by rebuilding pg from source against a system libpq (brew install libpq) — identical crash, so reverted that. "Self-heals via auto-restart" held in early testing but wasn't reliable — one real run sat crash-looping for over a minute. Real fix: bin/jobs start --mode=async runs the dispatcher/worker in bin/jobs's own process instead of forking children, never touching fork() at all, while staying its own OS process separate from Puma. Verified: enqueued a job from a separate process, confirmed the async worker executed it, zero crashes. Makefile and docker-compose.yml both updated to use --mode=async.

title: Sync per-game kinds off the season's game list directly, not one item per team
description: A whole-league sync_run (team: nil) creates one sync_run_item per team for game_stats/advanced_stats (PER_GAME_KINDS), and each item's games_for(team) matches home-or-away — so any two teams' games_for lists overlap on every game they played each other, and a shared game (e.g. ANA @ COL) gets fully reprocessed a second time once the later team's item comes up: a second network fetch, and for advanced_stats, a second full RebuildAdvancedStatsForGame pass rebuilding both teams' player chains and both teams' season rollups again. Wasteful on its own, and (per TASK-84) the second pass over an already-built chain is also the specific trigger that made PG::TRDeadlockDetected failures climb the deeper a run went. Real structural fix, not a patch: SyncRunItem.team is already optional (standings/daily_scores already run as a single team: nil item), and games_for(team) is already just Game.for_team(team).for_season(season)... — a filter on top of the season's full game list. So for PER_GAME_KINDS, stop fanning teams_for out into one item per team at all: build exactly one item (team: sync_run.team, i.e. nil for whole-league), and iterate Game.for_season(season).finished.chronological with the team filter applied only when sync_run.team is present. A game then physically cannot be visited twice in one run — no Set/tracking needed, and compute_total_steps stops double-counting shared games as a side effect (today's total_steps is roughly 2x actual unique games for a whole-league run). Only real wrinkle: run_per_game_item's step label currently reads "#{kind} — #{item.team.name} (i/count)", which breaks when item.team is nil for a whole-league item — switch it to name the actual matchup (e.g. "advanced stats — ANA @ COL (i/count)"), which is more informative anyway since it doesn't attribute a shared game to whichever team's turn it happened to be. Single-team-scoped runs are unaffected (same query, same one item, as today).

title: RecomputeSeasonStats issues 14-19 separate queries per player instead of one
description: Confirmed live in the dev log during a real season sync: RecomputeSeasonStats#upsert_skater computes a player's season totals via rows.count plus 13 separate .sum/.average calls (rows.sum(:goals), rows.sum(:assists), ... one full round trip to Postgres per column, all over the exact same row set) instead of one query — 14 queries total. #upsert_goalie is worse: 19 (games_played, games_started, goals, assists, wins/losses/ot_losses/shutouts as separate .where(...).count calls, plus 11 more .sum columns). Called once per player per game (SyncGameStats invokes it for every stat row a boxscore produces, ~40 players a game), so one game costs roughly 40 x ~15 queries ≈ 600 round trips for this step alone, before anything else — a real, measurable share of why a full-season sync is slow, not just perceived. Fix: pull the game rows once (rows.to_a, one query) and compute games_played/sums/counts/the faceoff-pctg average in plain Ruby from the materialized array instead of issuing a separate SQL aggregate per column — same output, ~14x fewer round trips. Care needed on faceoff_winning_pctg: SQL AVG skips NULLs, so the Ruby replacement needs to compact before averaging (and return nil, not NaN/0, when every row is nil) to match today's behavior exactly. No behavior/output change, pure query consolidation — safe to verify with the existing RecomputeSeasonStats spec plus the two SyncGameStats/SyncGameEvents specs that already exercise it indirectly.

title: Model franchise relocations/rebrands (e.g. Arizona Coyotes -> Utah Mammoth)
description: Real gap found seeding the 2023-24 NHL season: we only ever seeded the current-day "Utah Mammoth" Team row, so nothing from 2023-24 or earlier involving Arizona could resolve — missing_teams correctly reported "no team for ARI" rather than corrupting anything, but the season's data was silently incomplete for that one franchise. Confirmed against the real NHL API (2023-24 club-schedule-season response): Arizona's nhl_team_id was 53, Utah's is 68 — the NHL itself treats a relocation/rebrand as two distinct team ids, not one team renamed, which is why our nhl_team_id-as-natural-key convention finds nothing linking them. Decision made (see chat log): don't leave them as two silently-unrelated Team rows — model the link explicitly so the app can eventually show continuous franchise history across a move, rather than treating Utah's page as having no history before its first Utah game. Design: add_reference :teams, :predecessor_team, foreign_key: { to_table: :teams } (self-referential, nullable — most teams have none), Team belongs_to :predecessor_team, class_name: "Team", optional: true plus the inverse has_one :successor_team, and a validation rejecting a team naming itself and a predecessor from a different league (a franchise doesn't change leagues). Seed data: create the missing Arizona Coyotes Team row (nhl_team_id: 53) and set Utah's predecessor_team to it. Re-run the 2023-24 backfill afterward so Arizona's standings/schedule actually populate now that the row exists. Deliberately schema/model only for a first pass — serializer/frontend exposure (a team page showing "formerly the Arizona Coyotes") is a natural, separately-scoped follow-up once this lands, not required to close this out.

title: Batch RecomputeSeasonStats once per player for a bulk game_stats sync, not once per game
description: Confirmed against the real 2025-26 NHL season already in the dev DB: SyncGameStats#call recomputes every player's season stats after every single game (stats.each { |stat| recompute(stat) }), so a full-season bulk sync calls RecomputeSeasonStats once per game-stat row rather than once per player — 52,478 calls (47,231 skater + 5,247 goalie rows) where only 1,148 are actually needed (one per distinct player+team pairing, correctly covering a mid-season trade). ~46x more calls than necessary, stacking on top of TASK-86's ~14x fewer queries per call — roughly 640x more total round trips than needed for this step alone on a full historical backfill. Doesn't matter for a daily/incremental sync: with ~1 game per team a day, each player is only touched once regardless, so there's nothing to batch there — this is specifically a bulk-backfill inefficiency. Does NOT extend to advanced_stats: player_season_advanced_stats is intentionally a snapshot per game boundary (the player-detail chain feature depends on every intermediate row existing, not just the final total), so recomputing after every game is load-bearing there, not wasted work — this task is game_stats/RecomputeSeasonStats only. SyncGameStats has three callers: SyncGameStatsJob (single game, used for the daily case, correctly wants immediate recompute — leave as-is), AdminSyncOrchestrator's per-game game_stats item, and the nhl:backfill_game_stats rake task (both genuinely bulk, both carry the same waste). Fix belongs in the two bulk callers, not in SyncGameStats itself: call UpsertGameStats directly (skipping the recompute step SyncGameStats normally chains), track the distinct (player, team) pairs touched across the whole item/task run, then call RecomputeSeasonStats once per pair after the loop finishes rather than inside it. RecomputeSeasonStats itself needs no changes — it already re-derives wholesale from every game_stat row on file regardless of when it's called, so deferring the call is purely a scheduling change, not a correctness one.

title: Memoize Player/Team lookups in UpsertGameEvents and UpsertShifts
description: UpsertGameEvents#player_for and UpsertShifts#player_for both issue a fresh Player.find_by(nhl_player_id:) for every event/shift row, with no caching — same for the inline Team.find_by(nhl_team_id:) calls in both. Confirmed against a real game already in the dev DB (game 1947): 468 events and 1,363 shifts, but only 38 distinct players and 2 distinct teams ever involved. Current lookups: up to 1,404 Player.find_by calls for events (up to 3 players per play — primary/secondary/tertiary), 1,363 for shifts (one per row), and ~1,831 Team.find_by calls across both — roughly 4,600 avoidable queries for a single game. Across a full season (~1,400 games post-TASK-85) that's on the order of 6+ million avoidable queries — likely the single largest inefficiency in the whole sync pipeline, bigger than TASK-86 and TASK-88 combined. Checked ComputeGameAdvancedStats too (the next stage in the pipeline) and it's already clean — .includes(:player) on skater_shifts, works off raw FK ids rather than lazy-loaded associations, no N+1 there. This is isolated to the two upsert classes. Fix: memoize player_for (and a new team_for) in an instance-level hash in both UpsertGameEvents and UpsertShifts — both classes are already instantiated fresh per game (see SyncGameEvents#upsert_events/#upsert_shifts), so an instance-level cache is automatically scoped correctly with no cross-game staleness risk. Pure caching, no behavior change — the find_or_initialize_by(game:, nhl_event_id:)/nhl_shift_id: queries for the GameEvent/Shift rows themselves are unaffected and still needed, since each is genuinely distinct data.

title: One flaky per-game request fails the whole sync run, and the failure line can vanish from the log
description: Confirmed against a real run (sync run 20, whole-league game_stats, 1420 games): a single Socket::ResolutionError on one boxscore request (game 2023020528, a transient DNS blip) left the run reporting status: failed even though 1419/1420 games synced correctly and progress reached 1420/1420. Root cause in AdminSyncOrchestrator#run_per_game_item: the per-game rescue already does the right thing operationally — it logs the error and keeps iterating instead of aborting the run — but it also sets item failed = true unconditionally on any error, with no distinction between one flaky game and a systemic failure. #finalize! then treats any failed item as the whole run being failed, so a 1-in-1420 transient error and a run where every game failed look identical in sync_run.status. Compounding it: SyncRun#log caps activity_log to the last ACTIVITY_LOG_LIMIT entries, so the one 'Failed ...' line got pushed out by the ~1400 'Completed ...' lines that followed it — the item's error_message column was the only surviving trace, and nothing in the admin UI surfaces that column today. Net effect: a run can complete essentially cleanly and still alarm as failed, with no visible reason why. Two independent fixes, likely worth splitting: (1) give run_per_game_item real success/failure accounting — e.g. track failed game count vs total and only fail the item past some threshold, or always complete the item but record which specific games errored so they can be identified and retried individually; (2) either raise or remove ACTIVITY_LOG_LIMIT, or stop relying on activity_log for failure visibility at all and surface each item's error_message (and ideally which specific games failed, not just the last error) directly in the admin sync run view.

title: Distinguish partial failure from total failure in sync run/item status
description:
Deliberately deferred out of TASK-90: a per-game item's status is still binary — status: failed the moment any single game errors, whether it's 1 flaky game out of 1420 or every game failing outright. TASK-90 fixed the bigger problem (which games failed and why is now fully visible via failed_games), but the top-level status still can't tell those two situations apart at a glance. Fix would add a distinct status (e.g. completed_with_errors) or a threshold (e.g. fail the item only past some % of games erroring) — either way it's a new SyncRun::STATUSES value, which ripples into the frontend's SyncRunStatus type, badge rendering (SyncRunDetailPage, SyncDashboardPage), and any status-based filtering, so it's a real cross-stack change, not a quick add. Worth scoping properly (which of the two designs, where the threshold lives if any) rather than deciding inline.

Same issue exists one level up, found during a pipeline audit (Stage 2): AdminSyncOrchestrator#finalize! marks the whole SyncRun failed if any single item failed, even if e.g. game_stats fully succeeded and only advanced_stats had a couple of flaky games. Same binary-status problem, same fix shape — worth designing both levels together rather than as two separate changes later.

Done: added SyncRun::STATUSES[:completed_with_errors] (partial failure, distinct from total failure). Item level: run_per_game_item is completed only with zero failures, failed only when every game in scope failed, completed_with_errors otherwise. Run level: AdminSyncOrchestrator#finalize! mirrors the same three-way split across sync_run_items. Frontend: SyncRunStatus type + SYNC_RUN_STATUS_LABELS map, both status render sites updated, and useSyncRun's polling TERMINAL_STATUSES set was missing the new status (would have polled forever on a partial-failure run) — caught and fixed while wiring the frontend side.

title: Data tab: league/season sync coverage matrix, with gap-finding and invoke actions
description:
No way today to answer 'what have I actually synced' short of querying the DB directly — SyncRun history shows what runs were kicked off, not what data actually landed (a run can complete over already-fully-synced data, or fail partway and leave silent gaps). Confirmed real gaps this way while investigating: NHL 2023-24 has game_stats for 1215/1230 regular-season games (15 missing — 14 of them the entire 2023-12-23 slate plus 2 more from 12-27, almost certainly TASK-90's exact scenario: sync run 20's old error_message column only kept the last of several failures from one bad network window, silently losing the rest) and advanced_stats for 0/1230 (never run at all); meanwhile 2025-26 was already fully covered when a from-scratch advanced_stats re-run was kicked off against it, redundant work with no way to have known that in advance.

Shape (direct from conversation): a new 'Data' tab in the admin sidebar. Drills league -> season -> a table with one row per season and columns — games synced | roster synced | stats synced | advanced stats synced — each cell showing synced/total computed live from the actual data tables (Game, RosterSpot, SkaterGameStat, GameEvent, joined against Game.for_season/for_team), not from SyncRun rows, so it reflects ground truth regardless of how data got there (admin console, rake backfill, manual fix). Clicking a cell drills into the actual game list behind it — which specific dates/games are missing or errored, not just a count — exactly the kind of per-game breakdown TASK-90's failed_games groundwork already models, applied here to coverage gaps rather than run failures. Each cell also needs a way to invoke a full sync for that season/kind directly (reusing CreateSyncRun).

Also surface stale/stats_syncing counts per cell, not just row-exists coverage — confirmed live via TASK-94 that a cell can look 100% synced while a real chunk of it is quietly stale underneath (a cross-season backfill spuriously stale-marking another season's already-correct rows), which is invisible unless the matrix checks for it specifically, not just presence/absence of the row. Likely a new backend endpoint/serializer plus a frontend page under Admin, reusing DataTable/Card patterns already in the component library.

title: RebuildAdvancedStatsJob rebuilds a player's entire remaining-season chain per triggering game, not just the delta
description:
Confirmed live and actively blocking real use: after runs 21/22 (advanced_stats, 2024-25 and 2025-26 whole-league), the ingest queue had 737 backlogged RebuildAdvancedStatsJobs draining at ~1/minute — a 12+ hour backlog blocking two newly-queued sync runs (23, 24) from starting at all, since AdminSyncOrchestratorJob shares the same single-consumer ingest queue. Root cause, confirmed against a real backlogged job (job 1638, game 2706, an early October 2025-26 game): RebuildPlayerAdvancedStatsChain#rebuild_chain deletes and recreates every PlayerSeasonAdvancedStat row from the triggering game through the end of the season, for every affected player and every (strength_state, score_state) dimension. Because RebuildAdvancedStatsJob is enqueued async with no backpressure, ingestion (fast, ~4/sec at aggressive interval) races far ahead of the single-threaded recompute consumer — by the time an early-season game's job actually runs, hundreds of later games are already ingested, so 'rebuild from here to the end' means rebuilding hundreds of rows per player instead of the one new row actually needed. Confirmed: that sample job's rebuild covered 459 rows for one player alone. Every one of the 737 backlogged jobs does an overlapping version of this same bloated rebuild — genuine O(n^2) total work across a bulk sync, not O(n).

Not the same issue TASK-88 already addressed and explicitly excluded advanced_stats from — TASK-88 was about batching the *number of recompute calls*; this is about each individual call doing far more work than it needs to, regardless of how many calls there are. The fix likely isn't 'skip intermediate snapshots' (TASK-88's reasoning for why per-game snapshots are load-bearing still holds) but making the chain rebuild aware of how far ingestion has actually progressed — e.g. only extend the chain by rows that are actually new since the last rebuild for that player, or defer chain-rebuilding entirely until a bulk sync's ingestion phase is fully done and then walk each affected player's chain forward exactly once. Needs its own investigation before scoping a fix, not decided here. Real, currently-happening consequence: season-level PlayerSeasonAdvancedStat chains for 2025-26 are stale/incomplete until this backlog finishes draining, even though the underlying per-game data (GameEvent, PlayerGameAdvancedStat) is already complete and correct.

Implemented: MarkGameForStatsRecompute gained inline: false — true runs RebuildAdvancedStatsForGame synchronously instead of enqueueing RebuildAdvancedStatsJob, so ingestion can never race ahead of recompute (no algorithm change, same chain-rebuild logic, just no async detour). SyncGameEvents gained recompute_inline: false, passed through; AdminSyncOrchestrator's advanced_stats item passes recompute_inline: true.
