The single-game/live-correction path (SyncGameEventsJob) is untouched, still async. Verifying this against real data (2023-24, a season untouched by the still-draining backlog) surfaced a second, independent, pre-existing bug also fixed here: RebuildPlayerAdvancedStatsChain#ordered_rows filtered by game_type but not season_id, so a player with rows in multiple seasons (true for nearly every current player, since 2024-25/2025-26 were already ingested) pulled every season's same-game_type games into one chain and then failed PlayerSeasonAdvancedStat's season/as_of_game validation. This would have broken run 24 (2023-24 advanced_stats, queued behind the backlog) regardless of the inline fix, on the first cross-season player it hit. Both fixes verified together in a rolled-back real-data transaction: zero jobs enqueued, zero cross-season row leakage.

Remediation needed, not yet done (explicit choice, not an oversight): the season_id bug was live since early in this session, silently failing every cross-season chain rebuild it hit — confirmed via solid_queue_failed_executions: 1,456 distinct games with a failed RebuildAdvancedStatsJob (1,435 ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid from this exact bug, ~1,436 of them in 2024-25; the rest are old pre-TASK-84 deadlocks/connection drops). No corruption — every failure rolled back cleanly inside a transaction before any row committed — but real staleness: 2,415 games still stats_syncing: true, 135,551/333,495 PlayerSeasonAdvancedStat rows still stale: true. Fix is already live in the running worker (Rails dev autoloading picked it up without a restart, confirmed via new successful jobs after the fix with zero new failures) — closing the gap just needs the 1,456 already-failed SolidQueue::FailedExecution rows retried (SolidQueue::FailedExecution#retry, local recompute only, no NHL API calls, so not rate-limit-bound). Do this before considering 2024-25/2025-26 advanced stats fully trustworthy.

title: Decouple ingestion from season-chain rebuild for bulk/historical advanced_stats syncs
description:
Proposed directly by Adam, follow-up to TASK-93: RebuildPlayerAdvancedStatsChain and RecomputeTeamSeasonAdvancedStats are pure local-DB operations (read/write PlayerGameAdvancedStat/PlayerSeasonAdvancedStat/TeamGameAdvancedStat/TeamSeasonAdvancedStat, zero NHL API calls) — confirmed. ComputeGameAdvancedStats (the per-game Corsi/Fenwick/xG computation) is not the same thing and stays inline during ingestion either way; it's cheap, per-game, and is the raw data the chain later reads, not something to defer.

TASK-93 made the bulk path's chain rebuild synchronous instead of async, which fixed the crash/backlog-blowup risk, but each game's ingestion still waits on its own chain-rebuild write (destroy+recreate PlayerSeasonAdvancedStat rows for every affected player/dimension) before the next NHL fetch — bulk ingestion throughput is still bound by local DB compute, not just the NHL rate limit.

Proposed here: for bulk/historical syncs only (AdminSyncOrchestrator's advanced_stats item, whole-league or team-scoped), skip MarkGameForStatsRecompute entirely during the per-game ingestion loop — no stale-marking, no job, no inline call, just ComputeGameAdvancedStats per game and move on. Ingestion then runs purely NHL-rate-limited, exactly as fast as game_stats already does. After the whole bulk run finishes ingesting, a new batch step walks every distinct (player, season) and (team, season) touched by the run and calls RebuildPlayerAdvancedStatsChain / RecomputeTeamSeasonAdvancedStats exactly once each, using the earliest touched game as from_game — one clean linear pass per player/team covering the whole season's chain, replacing what would otherwise be hundreds of small per-game calls. Mirrors RecomputeTouchedSeasonStats's tracking pattern from TASK-88, applied to the chain-rebuild layer instead of the season-totals layer.

Daily/live single-game sync (SyncGameEventsJob) is unaffected and keeps today's per-game-immediate async behavior — already O(1) per call since it's never racing ahead of itself, and the live-correction use case (want stats_syncing visible immediately) still applies there. Needs care around game.stats_syncing/PlayerSeasonAdvancedStat.stale semantics during the ingest-only phase, since neither gets touched until the batch rebuild runs at the end — a season mid-backfill will show incomplete advanced-stat pages until that batch step completes, which is expected for a deliberate two-phase historical backfill but should be visible in the admin UI (ties into TASK-92's coverage matrix).

Implemented: SyncGameEvents/MarkGameForStatsRecompute's boolean inline flag replaced with a recompute: :async | :skip mode (the now-dead :inline case from TASK-93 removed, nothing calls it once the orchestrator moves to :skip). New RebuildTouchedAdvancedStatsChains tracks distinct player_ids/team_ids/game_ids touched during a bulk item's per-game loop; on #call, for each touched player it finds every (strength_state, score_state) dimension's own true earliest game for the season (not just the earliest game this particular run happened to touch first — a dimension introduced partway through, like a skater's first power-play shift, still needs its own correct anchor) and rebuilds from there, then recomputes each touched team's season rollup, then clears stats_syncing on every tracked game. AdminSyncOrchestrator wires this the same way as TASK-88's game_stats batch (tracked across the loop, flushed once in an ensure so a cancelled run still rebuilds whatever it touched). Also fixed in the same pass: MarkGameForStatsRecompute's stale-marking query had no season_id filter either (third instance of this exact bug class this session) — confirmed live, a 2023-24 backfill was spuriously marking a shared player's already-correct 2024-25/2025-26 rows stale (one sample player: all 333 2025-26 rows and all 18 2024-25 rows wrongly flagged). Verified end to end against real data: a rolled-back transaction against already-ingested 2024-25 games found McDavid had zero PlayerSeasonAdvancedStat rows at all for that season (a live instance of the 1,456-failed-job gap TASK-93 already flagged) — the new code correctly built his full real chain from scratch (60 games, 1639 Corsi-for, ~27.3/game, a plausible number for a top-line center) with zero jobs enqueued, then rolled back cleanly with zero rows left behind.

title: RecomputeTeamSeasonAdvancedStats issues 11 separate aggregate queries per dimension instead of one
description:
Found live while diagnosing why run 24 (advanced_stats, 2023-24) was only managing ~1 game per 14-30 seconds despite TASK-93's fix already making the player-chain rebuild correctly O(1) per game. RecomputeTeamSeasonAdvancedStats#upsert — the team-level counterpart called once per game for both teams via RebuildAdvancedStatsForGame — is the exact TASK-86 bug pattern in a class TASK-86 never touched: one count plus ten separate sum/average queries per (strength_state, score_state, game_type) dimension, re-summed from scratch off the entire season's TeamGameAdvancedStat rows every single call (not incremental), so cost grows as the season fills in.

Fixed identically to TASK-86: base_rows loaded once via .to_a (with game preloaded for game_type), dimensions and per-dimension sums/averages computed in Ruby via sum_of/average_of helpers, average_of NULL-skipping to match SQL AVG. Query-count regression spec added, same style as RecomputeSeasonStats's. Verified live and correctly: the currently-running AdminSyncOrchestratorJob for run 24 had already been executing before this fix landed (one continuous per-game loop inside a single job, not separate per-game jobs, so it never hit a Rails reload checkpoint) — required manually restarting the bin/jobs worker process for the fix to actually take effect, which in turn required manually clearing a stale SolidQueue::Process registration (the killed process's heartbeat hadn't been pruned yet, leaving its claimed job stuck instead of released) — both confirmed as expected Solid Queue mechanics, not new bugs.

title: Resumed sync run's progress counter never resets, can show over 100%
description:
Confirmed live: sync run 23 (game_stats, 2023-24) finished showing current_step=2045 of total_steps=1420 (144%). Root cause: AdminSyncOrchestrator#advance_step! does a raw increment (current_step = current_step + 1), and TASK-84's resume design re-runs a not-yet-completed per-game item wholesale from its first game when a job restarts (safe for data — every upsert is idempotent — but the step counter has no concept of a restart). Run 23's job was interrupted and resumed twice in one session: once for real (Solid Queue's own crash recovery after the worker process died, exactly as TASK-84 intends) and once from a deliberate bin/jobs restart to deploy the TASK-95 fix. Each restart re-looped all 1420 games from game 1, and increments from every pass landed on the same never-reset counter — three partial/full passes summing to ~1.44x the true total. No data risk (re-syncing an already-correct game just re-writes the same values), purely a progress-display bug.

Fix direction: on resume, current_step should be recomputed from real progress (e.g. count of items actually status: completed, or for a per-game item, some notion of games actually done) rather than blindly trusting a raw incrementing column that survives across restarts with no reset point. Possibly ties into TASK-90/91's broader theme of sync run status/progress not accurately reflecting reality across partial failures and resumes.

Done: AdminSyncOrchestrator#call now calls reset_current_step! on resume, before the loop starts — recomputes current_step from the real weight (step_weight, shared with compute_total_steps) of only status: completed items, since that's the exact condition the loop itself uses to decide what to skip vs. fully re-process. A running/failed/queued item contributes 0 to the reset baseline and gets recounted for real as it (re-)runs, so a crash-and-resume (or repeated resume) can no longer pile increments on top of a stale pre-crash total.

title: CreateSyncRun isn't atomic between saving the run and enqueueing its job
description:
Found during a front-to-back pipeline audit (Stage 1: entry point). CreateSyncRun#build_run saves the SyncRun row, then separately calls AdminSyncOrchestratorJob.perform_later(run.id). If the enqueue call ever raised after a successful save (Solid Queue enqueue is just a DB insert, so low likelihood, but not impossible — e.g. a connection blip to the queue database specifically), the SyncRun would be permanently stuck at status: queued with nothing ever processing it, and no error surfaced anywhere for an admin to notice. More idiomatic Rails fix: an after_create_commit callback on SyncRun itself that enqueues the job, rather than the service doing it as a separate manual step — makes the enqueue a property of the record existing, not an extra step that can be skipped/fail independently of the save.

Done: moved the enqueue into an after_create_commit callback on SyncRun itself; CreateSyncRun no longer calls AdminSyncOrchestratorJob.perform_later manually. Verified after_create_commit fires correctly under RSpec's transactional tests (existing request spec covers it).

title: Orchestrator: no sync_kinds dedup, a tracking-query failure can misreport as a sync failure, no mid-call cancellation for single-step items
description:
Three small, independent findings from a front-to-back pipeline audit (Stage 2: orchestration), none urgent. (1) Nothing dedupes SyncRun#sync_kinds — CreateSyncRun#resolve_kinds and AdminSyncOrchestrator#build_items both just iterate whatever's requested, so a run created with the same kind twice (API client bug, a future multi-select UI change) would build two identical items and double the API calls/local work for it. Low likelihood given the current frontend's fixed multi-select, but nothing actually prevents it. (2) AdminSyncOrchestrator#run_per_game_item's chain_batch&.track(game) call sits inside the same begin/rescue as the actual per-game sync call — if that tracking query itself hiccups (rare, but it's a real DB call), a game that genuinely synced fine gets recorded in failed_games with a confusing, unrelated error, conflating two different failure modes. (3) run_single_step_item has no mid-call cancellation check, unlike the per-game loop — a cancel request against a single-step item (roster/schedule/standings) only takes effect once that one service call returns, not during it. Low practical impact since those services are fast/atomic, but worth noting as an inconsistency with the per-game path's finer-grained cancellation.

Done, all three: (1) CreateSyncRun#resolve_kinds now .uniq's the resolved kind list. (2) run_per_game_item split into sync_game (the actual per-game sync call, rescued into failed_games) and track_game (recompute_batch/chain_batch tracking, rescued separately into an activity-log warning instead of failed_games) so a tracking hiccup no longer misreports a successful game as failed. (3) run_single_step_item left as-is with a comment documenting the accepted inconsistency — threading a cancellation check through every single-step service (SyncTeamRoster, SyncStandings, etc.) would be a real change to each of them for a low-impact case (those calls are already fast/atomic).

title: Five job classes have zero real callers: SyncTeamRosterJob, SyncAffiliateRosterJob, SyncTeamScheduleJob, SyncGameStatsJob, SyncGameEventsJob
description:
Found during a front-to-back pipeline audit (Stage 3: job/queue infra). Checked every job class in app/jobs against real callers across app/lib/config: AdminSyncOrchestratorJob (CreateSyncRun), RebuildAdvancedStatsJob (MarkGameForStatsRecompute's :async mode), PurgeRevokedTokensJob/SyncStandingsJob/SyncDailyScoresJob (all in recurring.yml) are genuinely wired. The other five — SyncTeamRosterJob, SyncAffiliateRosterJob, SyncTeamScheduleJob, SyncGameStatsJob, SyncGameEventsJob — have zero callers anywhere: AdminSyncOrchestrator calls their equivalent service classes directly (SyncTeamRoster.new(...).call, SyncGameStats.new(...).call, etc.) instead of enqueueing these wrapper jobs. SyncGameEventsJob even has a dedicated spec exercising dead code; SyncGameStatsJob doesn't have one at all.

Consequence worth flagging: this was assumed all session (including by earlier task write-ups today, e.g. TASK-93/94's own descriptions) to be 'the daily/single-game live-correction path' justifying MarkGameForStatsRecompute's :async default — but that path has no real caller today, so :async is currently unexercised in production, not actually load-bearing the way it was described.

Likely leftover from an earlier design where the admin console enqueued one job per record rather than AdminSyncOrchestrator calling services directly within its own single job (matches the same shape TASK-93/94 just deliberately chose for RebuildAdvancedStatsJob's bulk path, for the same reasons). Recommend deleting the 5 unused job files + the one orphaned spec — matches this codebase's own stated 'don't build speculatively' principle (see DECISIONS.md's DataTable entry) rather than carrying dead code forward.

Same root cause found again in Stage 5: SyncGameStats's default recompute: true branch ('the daily case, correctly wants immediate recompute') is also currently unexercised in production — its only caller for that default is SyncGameStatsJob, one of the five dead jobs here. Both AdminSyncOrchestrator and nhl:backfill_game_stats always pass recompute: false. Whatever replaces/removes the dead jobs should account for this branch too, not just SyncGameEvents's :async default.

Done: deleted the 5 dead job files (SyncTeamRosterJob, SyncAffiliateRosterJob, SyncTeamScheduleJob, SyncGameStatsJob, SyncGameEventsJob) and the orphaned SyncGameEventsJob spec. Updated SyncGameStats's recompute:true default comment to stop pointing at a now-deleted job.

title: NhlClient/NhlStatsClient/HockeyTechClient are ~90% duplicated code — extract a shared base client
description:
Found during a front-to-back pipeline audit (Stage 4: NHL API clients). The three external API clients (NhlClient for api-web.nhle.com, NhlStatsClient for the separate api.nhle.com shift-chart host, HockeyTechClient for the AHL/ECHL feed) are ~90% duplicated: the class-level throttle state (mutex, last_request_at accessor), #throttle, #monotonic_now, the #get retry-with-exponential-backoff wrapper, #perform's transport-error rescue (SocketError, SystemCallError, Net::OpenTimeout, Net::ReadTimeout -> TransportError), and the Error/NotFound/RateLimited/ServerError/TransportError exception hierarchy are all near-byte-identical across all three, roughly 50 duplicated lines each. Real, already-paid cost: the DEFAULT_MIN_INTERVAL change earlier this session had to be hand-applied to all three files separately, since nothing shares it. A BaseApiClient (throttle/retry/error-handling shared; each client supplies its own BASE_URL, endpoint methods, and response parsing) would cut ~120 duplicated lines and turn the next cross-cutting change into a one-file edit.

Smaller findings from the same stage, worth folding into the same cleanup pass rather than separate tasks: (1) #perform's rescue list doesn't catch OpenSSL::SSL::SSLError or EOFError, so those transient errors skip the built-in retry/backoff entirely — not silently swallowed (callers' broader StandardError rescues still catch them as a failed game/item), just missing the retry for that narrow class of error; a shared base client should widen this. (2) No persistent/keep-alive HTTP connection — Net::HTTP.start opens a fresh TCP+TLS handshake per request; currently masked by the enforced throttle interval (handshake cost is small next to a 0.25-1s wait) so low real-world impact today, but worth keeping a connection open across a client's requests if intervals ever get more aggressive. (3) NhlClient additionally duplicates its own retry logic between #get and #get_following_redirects within the same file, on top of the cross-file duplication.

A real, moderately-sized refactor (touches 3 well-tested classes with real callers throughout the sync pipeline) — not a quick inline fix, needs its own pass with full spec coverage carried over.

Done: extracted BaseApiClient (app/clients/base_api_client.rb) sharing throttle/mutex,
the with_retries wrapper, #perform's transport-error rescue (widened to also catch
OpenSSL::SSL::SSLError/EOFError per finding 1), and the Error/NotFound/RateLimited/
ServerError/TransportError hierarchy. Each subclass overrides path_for/request_params/
parse_body only where its shape differs (HockeyTechClient's fixed-path + query-folded
view + non-bare-JSON body). NhlClient's #get/#get_following_redirects now share one
with_retries instead of duplicating the retry loop (finding 3). Persistent-connection
(finding 2) explicitly deferred, documented inline. Net ~97 fewer lines across the
client layer. Verified: full spec suite (338 examples) unchanged, plus a live-network
smoke test against all three real APIs (standings, shift-chart, HockeyTech seasons,
a 307-redirect roster fetch, a real 404) and independent per-subclass throttle state
confirmed (separate Mutex objects). Logged in DECISIONS.md.

title: GoalieGamePoints#goals/#assists issue two separate queries instead of one
description:
Found during a front-to-back pipeline audit (Stage 5: basic stats ingestion). GoalieGamePoints#goals and #assists each re-evaluate the goal_events scope with their own separate query, called once or twice per goalie per game from UpsertGameStats#upsert_goalie — same pattern as TASK-86/95 (separate aggregate queries off the same relation) but at a scale bounded by goalies-per-game, not season size, so genuinely low priority. Fix: load goal_events once and derive both counts from the same in-memory rows.

Done: GoalieGamePoints now loads goal_events once (memoized array) and both #goals/#assists count over it in Ruby, instead of a separate AR query each. Added a query-count regression spec.

title: RecomputeGoalieGamePoints recomputes season stats once per game instead of once per distinct goalie/team
description:
Found during a front-to-back pipeline audit (Stage 6: season stats rollup). RecomputeGoalieGamePoints is called unconditionally from SyncGameEvents#call on every game, in every mode — not gated by the recompute: :async/:skip split TASK-94 added, so that fix didn't touch it. It calls RecomputeSeasonStats directly, once per goalie per game, completely bypassing TASK-88's RecomputeTouchedSeasonStats batch (which only wrapped SyncGameStats' path). Real cost: a full 2023-24 backfill (~1420 games x ~2 goalies) meant up to ~2,840 unbatched calls where the correct number is roughly 100-200 distinct (player, team, game_type) combos — same bug shape as TASK-88 (~15-25x here vs ~46x there, goalies being far fewer per game than skaters), actively firing on the live run at the time this was found.

Fixed the same way as TASK-88: RecomputeGoalieGamePoints gained recompute: :async (default, unchanged inline behavior) | :skip (updates each goalie's own goals/assists immediately but defers the season rollup, always returning the touched GoalieGameStat rows either way). SyncGameEvents passes its own recompute: value straight through and exposes the result via a new goalie_stats reader (call's own return value — events + shifts — was left untouched to avoid disturbing existing callers/specs). AdminSyncOrchestrator's PER_GAME_KINDS-shared RecomputeTouchedSeasonStats batch (previously game_stats-only) now also covers advanced_stats, tracking sync.goalie_stats the same way it already tracks SyncGameStats' rows.

Verified against real data: a rolled-back transaction against 3 already-ingested 2024-25 EDM games touched 12 goalie stat rows, zero RecomputeSeasonStats calls during the loop (correctly deferred), 8 calls after the batch flushed (real dedup, and exactly the skip-then-batch mechanism TASK-88 already proved at full-season scale).

title: Advanced-stats pipeline writes rows one at a time — no bulk upsert, GameEvent/Shift/PlayerGameAdvancedStat/TeamGameAdvancedStat/PlayerSeasonAdvancedStat all affected
description:
Found during a front-to-back pipeline audit (Stage 7: advanced stats ingestion, full-depth pass since TASK-89 already covered player/team lookups here; extended in Stage 8 after profiling ComputeGameAdvancedStats; extended again in Stage 9 profiling RebuildPlayerAdvancedStatsChain). All five models in this pipeline use find_or_initialize_by(...)/create! + #update!/#save! per row instead of a single bulk write. Measured against real data (2024-25, untouched by any in-progress run):

- UpsertGameEvents: 512 queries for 285 plays (~1.8/row)
- UpsertShifts: 1,481 queries for 720 shift rows (~2.06/row)
- ComputeGameAdvancedStats#persist_player_rows + #persist_team_rows: 618 queries for 206 rows (194 player + 12 team, ~3/row — PlayerGameAdvancedStat's own uniqueness validation stacks another query on top of find_or_initialize_by's lookup). This turned out to be the dominant cost of that whole class, not a minor one: profiled ComputeGameAdvancedStats#call end to end at ~400ms/game (accumulate_toi 25ms, accumulate_events 50ms — including on_ice_skater_ids' O(events x shifts) in-memory scan, the original suspect, which turned out small and not worth chasing — persist alone: 356ms, ~89% of the total).

- RebuildPlayerAdvancedStatsChain#rebuild_chain: 1,450 queries for one real player's (McDavid) full-season chain rebuild across 8 dimensions (~74 games) — TASK-94 already fixed the redundant-overlapping-rebuild problem (one call per player instead of one per game), but each row within that one call is still a separate PlayerSeasonAdvancedStat.create!, not a bulk insert. Since the accumulation (running_totals) is already computed sequentially in Ruby before each create!, batching the writes wouldn't require changing the computation at all — just collecting the built rows and inserting them together at the end of the loop.

Across a full ~1,400-game season: ~2.8 million queries for event/shift ingestion, ~865,000 queries (~8.3 min) for the game-level advanced-stat persist step, and plausibly 350,000-700,000 more for the season-chain persist step (~700-800 unique players, scaled from one real player's 1,450). Total plausibly 4-5 million queries across this whole family for one full-season sync.

Different shape of problem than the chain-rebuild bugs fixed earlier today (TASK-93/94/95/102): no cascading blowup, no multi-hour stalls — each query is cheap (sub-millisecond, indexed PK/unique lookup), just a large flat per-row multiplier. Still a real, now-fully-quantified cost worth fixing, not urgent enough to block anything.

Not a safe drop-in fix for any of the five: GameEvent/Shift have real validations (team_played_in_game, end_after_start, uniqueness scoped to game, inclusion checks); PlayerGameAdvancedStat has its own uniqueness validation; PlayerSeasonAdvancedStat has the most validations of all (uniqueness across 5 columns, team_belongs_to_season_league, as_of_game_belongs_to_season, game_type_matches_as_of_game) — and as_of_game_belongs_to_season is the exact validation that caught TASK-93/94's real season_id bug earlier today, so this one specifically has already proven its value once; any bulk-write fix here needs to replicate equivalent protection in Ruby, not just drop it. Rails' bulk-upsert tools (upsert_all/insert_all) skip ActiveRecord validations and callbacks entirely, operating at raw SQL. Needs its own properly-scoped design pass, likely one that covers all five models together since they share the exact same pattern and fix shape.

Done, all five models via one shared BulkUpsert (Ruby pre-validate + insert_all, per user's chosen direction): each model's uniqueness validator gained on: %i[create update] so BulkUpsert's own :bulk_upsert validation context skips it (an unsaved instance has no id to exclude itself, so re-checking uniqueness there would wrongly reject a legitimate update to an already-existing row) while every other validation — presence, inclusion, and every custom business-rule check (team_played_in_game, end_after_start, team_belongs_to_season_league, as_of_game_belongs_to_season, game_type_matches_as_of_game) — still runs in Ruby before the row is allowed into the batch. The DB's own unique index (confirmed already present and matching for all five) is what upsert_all's on-conflict match relies on instead. UpsertGameEvents/UpsertShifts build unsaved instances and gained a failures reader (same idea as missing_players); ComputeGameAdvancedStats now preloads game.home_team/away_team and skater_shifts' already-loaded player objects so no association read during validation costs its own query; RebuildPlayerAdvancedStatsChain now preloads team/game on ordered_rows for the same reason, and raises (rolling back the whole chain, matching create!'s old fail-hard behavior) if BulkUpsert reports any failure — a bad row there is corruption risk, not routine noise, since this is the exact validation class that caught a real bug before (TASK-93/94).

Verified against real data (game id=1, untouched by any in-progress run), rolled-back transaction, output confirmed byte-identical to the pre-change rows: full per-game SyncGameEvents (events + shifts + player/team advanced stats together) dropped from a combined ~2,600+ queries to 122 (~95% reduction). Individually: UpsertGameEvents+UpsertShifts (1,064 rows) 89 queries; ComputeGameAdvancedStats persist step (257 rows) 21 queries. RebuildPlayerAdvancedStatsChain (Marner, full 960-row season chain) dropped to 225 queries. Backend suite (320 examples) and RuboCop both clean before this change; new/updated specs cover BulkUpsert directly (valid+invalid rows, update-not-reject-as-duplicate) and each service (one INSERT statement per table instead of one per row, plus the rollback-on-invalid-row behavior for the season chain).

title: Batch recompute steps have no per-item error isolation — one bad player/team crashes the whole run
description:
Found during a front-to-back pipeline audit (Stage 9: the rebuild/recompute family). AdminSyncOrchestrator#run_per_game_item's batch steps (recompute_batch via RecomputeTouchedSeasonStats, chain_batch via RebuildTouchedAdvancedStatsChains, and RecomputeTeamSeasonAdvancedStats called within it) all run inside the method's ensure block with no per-item rescue. This is a real robustness gap the batching work introduced as a side effect (TASK-88/94/102): the old per-game-trigger design had each game's own recompute wrapped in that game's own begin/rescue (the same one that populates failed_games), so one bad row was isolated and recorded. Moving the recompute to one end-of-run batch call lost that isolation — if even one player's chain rebuild or one team's rollup raises (out of what can be hundreds in a full-season run), the exception propagates straight out of ensure, past run_item, past the orchestrator's outer item loop, uncaught, crashing the entire Solid Queue job. The run never reaches finalize!, gets stuck at status: running until TASK-84's crash-recovery eventually notices and the job gets re-queued — meaning one bad edge case in one player's data forces re-running every game in the item from scratch, not just recording one failure.

No evidence this has actually happened yet, but the failure mode is real and the blast radius is large (a whole item's worth of already-completed ingestion work, not one game). Fix: wrap each batch item's individual rebuild call in its own rescue inside RecomputeTouchedSeasonStats#call/RebuildTouchedAdvancedStatsChains#call, recording failures (ideally surfaced the same way failed_games already is) instead of letting one bad row abort the whole batch.

Done: both RecomputeTouchedSeasonStats#call and RebuildTouchedAdvancedStatsChains#call now rescue each individual row (per player/team combo) internally, collecting messages in a new #failures reader instead of letting one bad row abort the whole batch uncaught. Side effect fixed for free: RebuildTouchedAdvancedStatsChains previously never reached its Game#stats_syncing reset if any player raised, leaving those games stuck stats_syncing: true forever — now reached regardless. AdminSyncOrchestrator#run_per_game_item's ensure block calls each batch through a new run_batch wrapper that also rescues the batch's own setup query (not just per-row) and logs every failure via sync_run.log, so a bad batch no longer crashes the job before finalize! runs.

title: Historical/bulk advanced_stats syncs never got a follow-up season-rollup recompute for already-ingested seasons
description:
TASK-94 deliberately decoupled bulk ingestion from season-chain rebuild so historical backfills could pull NHL data fast without paying the recompute cost per game. That decoupling was intentionally used for at least 2024-25: ingestion (game_events/shifts/PlayerGameAdvancedStat/TeamGameAdvancedStat) is fully complete for that season, but the season-rollup step (PlayerSeasonAdvancedStat) was never separately triggered afterward — no task was created to close that loop. Confirmed real, not a display bug: John Tavares (and the wider league) has real per-game advanced-stat rows for 2024-25 but zero PlayerSeasonAdvancedStat rows for it; across the whole season, 1,336 players have per-game rows but only 422 have any season rollup at all (≈32% coverage). Matches the stats_syncing/stale backlog already flagged for 2024-25 earlier this session (1,436 games stuck stats_syncing: true, 1,301 stale rows).

Fix needs a way to run the batched rebuild (RebuildTouchedAdvancedStatsChains, TASK-94/104's design) against already-ingested seasons without re-hitting the NHL API — the existing rake advanced_stats:backfill task recomputes from stored data already (no API calls) but predates TASK-94's batching: it calls RebuildPlayerAdvancedStatsChain once per game a player appears in instead of once per player for the whole season, so it would work but slower than necessary. Needs its own properly-scoped implementation, likely a new rake task or admin action built on RebuildTouchedAdvancedStatsChains directly, scoped to a season.

Done: built ComputeIndividualGameStats (faceoff wins/losses, shots attempted/missed/blocked-against, derived from game_events already ingested — no NHL API calls), wired into SyncGameEvents and AdminSyncOrchestrator's batch path, extended RecomputeSeasonStats to roll the new fields up. Added a new self-service rebuild_season_stats sync kind (queueable/monitorable from the existing admin dashboard, re-runnable any time a new stat calc needs backfilling into an already-synced season) alongside a rake task (advanced_stats:rebuild_season) for the same thing without a browser.

Found and fixed a second, more serious bug along the way: RebuildTouchedAdvancedStatsChains#dimension_start_games anchored each dimension's rebuild at the chronologically-earliest touched game without filtering by game_type — preseason/regular/playoff games all share one season_id, so any player with preseason advanced-stat data got their entire season chain silently redirected to a preseason-only rebuild, never touching the real regular-season rollup. Confirmed live: 100% correlation between 'has preseason data' and 'got a bogus preseason row' in 2024-25 (1,272/1,272). Fixed by scoping the anchor-game lookup by game_type too.

Verified end to end against real production data: after fixing the bug, cleaning up ~42K bogus preseason rows, and re-running the (fixed) rebuild for both 2024-25 and 2025-26 — both seasons reached 100% regular-season coverage (886/886 and 940/940 players with real per-game advanced stats now have a real season rollup), 0 stale rows, 0 games stuck stats_syncing. New individual stats populated on 97%+ of SkaterSeasonStat rows for both seasons.
